headline: US midterms underway as the RBA hikes rates to an 18-year high — a big day for politics on both sides of the Pacific.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: GTA 6 hype is driving strong momentum last night — pre-loading was moved up to November 10th and the release date of November 19 is confirmed. Investors are pricing in a massive launch. The stock is still down ~9% overall from your entry, but the long-term thesis around GTA 6 is playing out exactly as expected.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped last night after strong FY27 Q1 earnings results, with Azure cloud revenue continuing to beat expectations. Analysts are highlighting Microsoft as the clear winner in the AI spending race among the big cloud providers — more businesses are choosing Azure to run their AI workloads.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped today, tracking weakness in some of its AI holdings. Broader concerns about whether AI company valuations can be justified — flagged in a Reuters piece today — are weighing on sentiment. Nothing broken with the long-term AI story, but it's a bumpy ride.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: A small bounce today for PLS, but the big news this week is Citi slashing its lithium price forecast by 40% on weaker-than-expected battery demand. That's a real headwind for the whole sector. PLS is still deep in the red overall — the lithium recovery is taking much longer than the market hoped.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped slightly last night. Seeking Alpha flagged that recent earnings raised 'serious concerns' about Google Search revenue growth as AI-powered competitors chip away at its core business. Wall Street is lowering its revenue bar for Search — that's not a great sign, though the long-term diversification story (YouTube, Cloud, AI) keeps the thesis alive.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Essentially flat today — tiny dip, nothing to read into it. VDHG tracks a globally diversified basket of assets, so the day-to-day moves are usually just noise. Sits just slightly below your cost base overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: A minor dip today on the ASX, reflecting the AUD pricing of US market exposure. The underlying US market (S&P 500 and NASDAQ) were both up last night, so this is mainly a currency effect — the Aussie dollar fell today, which can cause slight mismatches in how ASX-listed US ETFs price.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Virtually flat today. Emerging markets continue to face headwinds from a stronger US dollar and softer global growth expectations. No specific news driving the move — just background noise.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: As flat as it gets — essentially unchanged today. DHHF holds a wide mix of global shares, so single-day moves this small are meaningless. Long-term, this is doing its job as a diversified core holding.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 pre-loading moved up — TTWO momentum building
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 pre-loading kicks off November 10 (that's one week away), with the full release on November 19. The game requires 212 GB of storage and is already generating massive buzz. This is the biggest catalyst in Take-Two's history — your TTWO position is still down ~9% overall, but the long-term thesis is intact and on the verge of its defining moment. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Microsoft earnings beat — strong AI tailwind
watch_today.detail: MSFT jumped +1.37% last night after smashing FY27 Q1 expectations, driven by Azure cloud and AI workloads. Your MSFT position is now up +16% overall. Nothing to do here — this is exactly the long-term story you bought into. Hold with confidence.

watch_today.title: Citi cuts lithium forecast 40% — watch PLS closely
watch_today.detail: Citi slashed its lithium price forecast by 40% this week, citing weaker battery demand growth. Australian lithium stocks slid on the news. PLS bounced slightly today (+0.77%) but is still down ~61% from your entry. The structural case for lithium long-term remains (EVs, batteries) but the recovery timeline keeps getting pushed out. Unless something changes fundamentally, hold — don't add at this stage.

watch_today.title: RBA hikes rates to 18-year high — impact on your portfolio
watch_today.detail: The RBA lifted interest rates again today, taking them to their highest level since 2008. The board warned inflation will be painful for at least another year. Higher rates tend to weigh on growth stocks and ETFs with heavy equity exposure. Watch for any flow-on effects this week — but for a long-term holder, this isn't a reason to sell anything.

watch_today.title: Google Search concerns — GOOG under pressure
watch_today.detail: Post-earnings analysis flagged serious concerns about Google Search revenue growth, with AI-powered rivals taking market share. Wall Street is lowering its revenue bar for Search. Your GOOG holding is down ~9.8% overall. The long-term case (YouTube, Cloud, Gemini AI) is still intact, but this is worth keeping an eye on over the next few quarters. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: GXAI dip — AI sentiment wobble, not a structural break
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 2.57% today, its sharpest single-day drop in a while. Reuters flagged broader concerns about whether the AI spending boom could destabilise global markets. That said, your underlying AI companies (Microsoft etc.) are still growing strongly. GXAI is down ~17.8% overall from your entry — painful, but the long-term AI growth story hasn't changed. Hold.

world.summary: The US midterm elections are the dominant global story today, with voting underway and Trump already casting doubt on results. Meanwhile, the US has struck Iran's Qeshm Island while diplomatic talks continue, adding tension to an already fragile geopolitical environment.

stories.title: US Midterm Elections Underway — Trump Sowing Doubt on Results
stories.why_it_matters: Americans are voting in the midterm elections today — the first major electoral test of Trump's current presidency. There's been a surge in early voting, and Trump is already publicly casting doubt on the legitimacy of results, including launching a court appeal over California ballot counting. The outcome will determine whether Republicans maintain control of Congress, which directly shapes Trump's ability to pass legislation on taxes, trade and foreign policy over the next two years. Markets are watching closely — a split Congress could limit Trump's agenda.

stories.title: US Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Trump Talks Down War Risks
stories.why_it_matters: The US military has struck Iran's Qeshm Island — a significant escalation — even as Trump publicly plays down the risk of a full-blown war. Iran's foreign minister says intensive talks with mediators are ongoing, and Qatar says it expects a response within 36 hours on a potential deal. The dual-track of military strikes and diplomacy is creating serious uncertainty — oil prices above $96 a barrel reflect some of that tension. If talks collapse, expect oil to spike and markets to wobble.

stories.title: Iran Signals It Wants a Deal — But Says It's Still Distant
stories.why_it_matters: Trump told reporters Iran 'wants a deal and it could happen,' while Iran's side says any US agreement remains distant. Qatar is acting as mediator and is expecting a formal reply from Tehran within 36 hours. The mixed signals are keeping markets on edge — if a deal happens, oil prices could fall sharply (good for inflation globally); if not, the military conflict could escalate further.

stories.title: Reuters: Big AI Bets Could Break Already Fragile Global Markets
stories.why_it_matters: Reuters published a major analysis warning that the massive wave of corporate investment into AI infrastructure — data centres, chips, power — is creating concentrated risks in already stretched global financial markets. The concern is that if AI revenue doesn't materialise fast enough to justify the spending, a pullback could trigger a broader market correction. For anyone holding AI-exposed stocks or ETFs (like GXAI, MSFT, GOOG), this is the key long-term risk to understand.

stories.title: Japan Launches New Dedicated Disaster Agency
stories.why_it_matters: Japan has officially launched a new national disaster preparedness agency, a direct response to the country's repeated experience with earthquakes, tsunamis, and typhoons. The agency will centralise disaster planning and emergency response across government departments. Japan is one of the world's most disaster-prone nations, and this kind of institutional reform matters for regional stability — it's also a signal to other Pacific nations, including Australia, about the value of dedicated disaster governance.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 0.34% to 8,887. Last night on Wall Street, the NASDAQ led gains (+0.71%) as Microsoft's strong earnings lifted tech broadly. The S&P 500 edged up 0.30%. Oil is sitting just above $96 a barrel amid the Iran tensions, and gold dipped slightly. The Aussie dollar fell about 0.66% against the USD to around 69.8 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today, buoyed by global tech optimism and strong overnight leads.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's gain — modest but steady, supported by Microsoft's earnings beat.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech led the charge last night, with Microsoft the standout mover.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Eased slightly despite Iran tensions — market weighing diplomacy vs. military escalation.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Pulled back a little — risk appetite improved on the back of positive earnings.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar slipped after today's RBA rate hike — traders adjusting expectations.

politics.summary: The RBA hiked interest rates again today to their highest level since 2008, warning that inflation will remain elevated for at least another year. The Albanese government is facing questions about whether its spending has added to the inflation problem.

stories.title: RBA Hikes Rates to 18-Year High, Warns Inflation Will Hurt for Another Year
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Board raised the cash rate again today, pushing it to its highest point since 2008. The board warned that inflation will remain painful for at least another year and that more hikes may be needed. For mortgage holders, this means another increase in monthly repayments — a family with a $600,000 variable-rate mortgage can expect to pay hundreds of dollars more per month compared to two years ago. Savers get a slightly better deal on term deposits, but anyone with debt is feeling the squeeze. The big four banks had not yet passed on the rate increase as of this afternoon.

stories.title: Has Government Spending Fuelled Inflation? Charts Tell the Story
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News published a detailed chart-driven analysis asking whether Labor's spending has contributed to Australia's inflation problem. This is a politically charged question heading into the next election cycle — the Opposition has been hammering the government on this, and today's rate hike will reignite the debate. The charts suggest government spending has played some role, though the RBA's own statement points to global supply factors and a tight labour market as the main drivers.

stories.title: Labor Accused of $170 Billion Budget Black Hole
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian is running a story claiming Labor is sitting on a secret $170 billion budget shortfall — a 'black hole' the government hasn't publicly disclosed. If accurate, this would significantly constrain Labor's ability to deliver election promises and keep the budget in surplus. The government has not confirmed the figures, and the story comes from The Australian, which has been critical of Labor's fiscal management. Worth watching as more details emerge ahead of the next budget update.

stories.title: EV Tax Break Under Fire as 112,000 Drivers Blow the Budget
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that 112,000 Australian drivers have taken up the government's electric vehicle fringe benefits tax (FBT) exemption — far more than budgeted — and calls are growing to scrap or cap the scheme. The EV tax break allows employees to salary-sacrifice an EV and pay no FBT, saving thousands of dollars. The blowout in take-up means it's costing the budget significantly more than projected, and with inflation still hot and the budget under pressure, critics argue it's poorly targeted and expensive.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a split emerging in the industry — with Meta and Palantir pushing for open-source AI on one side, and OpenAI, Anthropic and Google backing tighter controls on the other. Meanwhile, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is competing hard on value, and an EU court adviser has raised copyright concerns about Google's AI chatbot.

stories.title: The Great AI Rift: Meta & Palantir vs OpenAI, Anthropic & Google
stories.why_it_matters: A major philosophical and business divide is opening up in the AI industry. Meta (Facebook's parent) and Palantir are pushing for open-source AI — where the underlying code is freely available for anyone to build on. On the other side, OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude) and Google (Gemini) want more controlled, proprietary approaches with tighter safety guardrails. This fight matters because it will determine who controls AI technology in the coming decade — open systems could democratise AI but also make it harder to regulate, while closed systems keep power concentrated with a handful of companies.

stories.title: EU Court Adviser Says Google's AI Chatbot May Infringe Copyright
stories.why_it_matters: An adviser to the EU's top court has said that Google's AI chatbot (Gemini) likely infringes on press publishers' copyright by using news articles in its responses without proper licensing. This is a significant legal opinion — EU court advisers' opinions are followed by the court in most cases. If it becomes binding, Google could be forced to pay licensing fees to news publishers across Europe, adding costs to its AI business and potentially changing how AI chatbots source information. GOOG holders should note this as an emerging regulatory risk.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Competitive in AI Benchmarks, Wins on Value
stories.why_it_matters: Google's latest Gemini 4 Carbon model is scoring just behind Anthropic's Claude on industry benchmarks — but beating it on value, meaning you get more capability for the cost. This is important for businesses choosing which AI to build products on. Google keeping pace (and winning on price) helps justify its massive AI investment and is a positive signal for GOOG shareholders watching the Gemini product line compete against OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.title: Google Rounds Up October 2026 AI Announcements
stories.why_it_matters: Google's official blog published a roundup of all its AI announcements from October 2026 — a useful snapshot of how fast the company is shipping new AI features across Search, Workspace (Gmail, Docs), Maps, and its cloud business. The volume of updates signals Google is moving quickly to defend its turf against Microsoft and OpenAI, particularly in enterprise software where Microsoft has been gaining ground.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is the big local result — the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. Off the field, the Josh Addo-Carr drugs saga continues, and NRL clubs are being valued at record highs.

stories.title: Roosters Win NRL Grand Final 19-18 Over Knights in a Thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters defeated the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a nail-biting NRL Grand Final at Accor Stadium. One point separated the two teams at the final whistle — it doesn't get closer than that in a decider. The Roosters claim the premiership in what will be remembered as one of the great Grand Finals.

stories.title: Josh Addo-Carr Speaks Out: $400k Drugs Test Ordeal 'Changed My Life'
stories.why_it_matters: Parramatta Eels star Josh Addo-Carr has broken his silence on his drugs testing saga, revealing the ordeal cost him $400,000 and 'changed his life.' Addo-Carr says the stress and financial hit from the case was enormous. The case took a 'shock turn' this week ahead of Eels internal meetings, though details remain unclear. It's one of the most significant off-field controversies in the NRL this season.

stories.title: AFL and NRL Club Brands Valued at Combined $2.9 Billion
stories.why_it_matters: Brand Finance's 2026 report has valued all AFL and NRL club brands at a combined $2.9 billion — a record high. Collingwood has overtaken the NRL's powerhouse clubs to become the most valuable football brand in Australia. The figures show the enormous commercial scale of Australian football codes, with clubs increasingly operating as proper media and entertainment businesses, not just sporting teams.

stories.title: Benji Marshall's Coaching Shake-Up: New Faces Join Tigers Staff
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers coach Benji Marshall is shaking up his coaching staff heading into the off-season, with new names joining the set-up. The Tigers have been rebuilding for several seasons and the reshuffle signals Marshall is serious about making the next step. A Premier League club has also paid tribute to former Tigers player Jacob Arrow, adding an international flavour to what's been a big week for the club.
